subject: accordion
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: piano accordion.
Style: Italian mother-of-pearl.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static piano accordion prop with an Italian mother-of-pearl aesthetic, keeping the geometry compact and efficient using basic part shapes like extrusions and lathes, with real-world proportions in mind.

I'm orienting the model with the bellows running horizontally along the X axis, a treble box on one end and a bass box on the other, standing upright at roughly 0.40m tall, with the piano keyboard mounted vertically on the front face of the treble box.

I'll orient keys like a piano on its side, with key tops facing outward and white/black key blocks sized small relative to the treble box. Now I'm defining the treble box body dimensions and giving it a pearl-white, mother-of-pearl finish.

For the pearl look, I'll use a mottled pastel paint blend of pearl white and soft teal across the body, with chrome/gold trim and red bellows accented in white and gold at the corners. I'm now planning the bellows as a series of folded frustum slabs along the x-axis, alternating widths to create an accordion-like pleated structure.

I'll add small gold corner accents at the four edges of each ridge for detail, and define the bellows cross-section dimensions with deep red ridges and darker red valleys. Then I'm starting to lay out the bass box dimensions on the left side.

For the bass side, I'm planning a visible button grid of 60 pearl buttons (6 columns × 10 rows) as short cylinders, and considering merging the geometries using BufferGeometryUtils to stay under the part limit, though I'm a bit unsure about the import path reliability.

Still working out button layout...

Now for the end plates: the treble box's outer face gets a decorative grille with gold perforated slats and a pearl surround, while the bass side could use a leather strap loop on its outer end.

I'll add shoulder-strap fittings to the back of the treble box, a row of pearl-and-gold register switches on its top face near the keyboard, and a thin gold trim frame running along the edges of both boxes using a reusable frame-building helper. Behind the keys I'm placing a dark recessed key-bed plate.

Now I'm working out the keyboard layout: 24 white keys spaced along the treble box front face, with gold guard rails on either side, and deciding where to position the shorter black keys relative to the white ones.

For color, white keys are an ivory shade while black keys are near-black with a tiny mother-of-pearl inlay accent on top, following the natural ascending note pattern from bottom to top.

I'm thinking through adding a mottled pearl paint effect to the box surfaces, plus a decorative border of small flattened diamond shapes scattered along the front edges in alternating pastel colors, built via a helper function that places them in a repeating row.

I also want a gold medallion badge above the bass box buttons, extruded as a cartouche ellipse with a pearl center and tiny gem accent, positioned carefully above the button rows so it doesn't overlap them.

I'll add a small pearl nameplate texture reading "ITALIA" on it. For a carrying handle, I'm considering a leather sweep arching over the top of the bass box using a catmull-spline path, though I need to check whether sweep geometry works properly without joint connections on a static model.

Adding handle arch points...

Checking box edge positions against bellows width to decide whether a strap would clip through the pleat ridges—deciding to skip it and just terminate the strap ends on the boxes instead.

Now I'm working out the bellows gap geometry, spacing twelve ridges evenly across the width with thin plate shapes sitting outside a single core box, plus gold corner binding strips for the pleat look.

Adding corner brackets and frame plates...

Now I'm sizing the boxes and bellows: boxes get height 0.40 starting at y=0.012 to leave room for small rubber feet, with bellows sharing the same vertical center but slightly shorter. I'm also placing the keyboard bed on the treble box's front face.

Working out the keyboard details now: a dark felt plate sits on the face, with white key boxes layered on top and black keys positioned above and slightly offset toward the bellows side.

I'm computing the vertical spacing for the 24 white keys and the gold rail boxes that flank the keybed at top and bottom, aligning their positions with small margins to fit neatly within the overall layout.

For the treble end, I'm leaving pearl-faced side columns beside the centered keys, then designing a gold grille panel for the +X end with vertical slats and a pearl medallion, plus planning register switches along the top face above the keyboard.

Now I'm laying out five rectangular pearl switch pads in a row on the top face with dark slots beneath, then adding a bass-end carrying handle and leather strap with gold buckle and pearl diamond details, and defining the color palette for pearl, pink, lilac, and aqua tones.

Setting up mottled paint textures for the body combining pearl and contrasting tones, importing the mottle utility for use on both bass and treble finishes.

Writing geometry helpers...

Still writing frame edge helpers...

Now I'm laying out the bass button grid, an 8×11 array of small cylinders colored mostly ivory with occasional marker rows picked out in a contrasting pearl tone.

Checking the badge placement fits within the cartouche bounds under the top trim, then adding diamond trim columns flanking both the bass and treble button grids, keeping margins consistent with the gold rails.

Still placing decorative elements...

Adding a diamond-ring accent around the medallion, then moving to the bass end with a leather strap plate, stitching details, buckle, and a pearl cap with diamond ring. I'm also considering a small leather back strap pad near the treble end for added detail.

Now I'm placing the actual strap boxes with gold buckle bits, plus shoulder-strap D-ring toruses on the treble back. I'm adding rubber feet cylinders under each box corner, and working out the bellows corner bracket depths and ridge plate positions.

For the bellows core and ridge plates I'm alternating red tones for visual variety, and adding pearl-and-gold corner brackets at each ridge junction to mimic the real accordion's decorative trim.

I'm placing dark end-frame plates with gold edges at the bellows' outer boundaries, slightly overlapping the ridge stack for a seamless look, then sweeping a leather-colored handle along a curved path on the bass side.

Now I'm adding small gold cylinder mounts at the handle ends, a pearl strip near the treble register switches, a diamond accent band on the bass top, and a tiny gold air-button cylinder near the bass front.

Setting up positional constants for the box bodies, then building the box geometries with pearl paint and gold trim frames around each side using these dimensions.

For the diamond bands, I'm working out placement on the bass front columns using a vertical diamond lattice pattern, and skipping areas near the keybed and buttons where they'd overlap. I'm also planning a pearl mosaic diamond lattice for the back faces of the boxes.

Now I'm working out the key layout itself, placing ivory keys at regular intervals along the treble side.

For the black keys, I'm positioning them at the correct pentatonic offsets within each octave, giving them a slightly raised position above the white keys, then adding a thin pearl inlay strip on top of each for detail.

I'm adding a red felt bed beneath the keys, then placing gold rails along the top and sides to frame the keybed, checking that each box's dimensions keep it within the base boundaries.

Now I'm laying out the register switch panel at the top: a slot plate, five alternating pearl/pink switches with small gold caps, positioning them so the top edge aligns exactly with the case height.

I'm adding gem spheres on the bass side, positioning the grille, and setting up a flat-shaded octahedron helper for diamond shapes using scaled geometry. I'm also writing the loop that generates the bass button grid with staggered rows and columns.

Now I'm defining the ring marker and button cylinders for each row, choosing black accents on certain rows versus ivory elsewhere, then placing the leather strap and gold buckle frame on the bass end.

Writing buckle geometry...

Then I'll finalize with the metadata, naming the piece "Piano Accordion" and writing its description.
